## What VAPOR does

VAPOR jointly estimates, in a single Gibbs sampler:

- **B**, the VAR(1) coefficient matrix (the dynamics), and
- **Omega**, the precision matrix of the innovations, modeled as a low-rank
  plus diagonal factor structure (`Omega = Lambda Lambda' + Delta`).

The two are estimated together: the coefficient update is GLS-transformed by the
current precision, and the precision is estimated from the current residuals.
This is aimed at the high-dimensional regime where the number of series `p` is
close to the number of time points `T`, where a plain VAR overfits and the
sample covariance is not invertible.

```{r setup}
library(VAPOR)
set.seed(1)
```

## Simulate data

We generate `T = 120` observations of `p = 40` series from a VAR(1) with a
low-rank-plus-diagonal innovation precision, so we know the true `Omega`.

```{r simulate}
p <- 40; T <- 120; k_true <- 3

# true innovation precision: Lambda Lambda' + diagonal
Lambda_true <- matrix(rnorm(p * k_true, 0, 0.6), p, k_true)
Delta_true  <- diag(runif(p, 0.5, 1.5))
Omega_true  <- Lambda_true %*% t(Lambda_true) + Delta_true
Sigma_true  <- solve(Omega_true)

# true VAR(1) dynamics: a stable, mildly persistent B
B_true <- matrix(rnorm(p * p, 0, 0.03), p, p); diag(B_true) <- 0.3

# simulate
chol_S <- chol(Sigma_true)
Y <- matrix(0, T, p)
for (t in 2:T) {
   eps <- as.numeric(crossprod(chol_S, rnorm(p)))
   Y[t, ] <- B_true %*% Y[t-1, ] + eps
}
Y <- scale(Y)
dim(Y)
```

## Fit VAPOR

The main entry point is `vapor()`. For `T` close to `p`, use the reduced-rank
parameterization (`rank = r`) with the default Dirichlet-Laplace prior on the
VAR coefficients. `k` is the number of precision factors.

```{r fit}
fit <- vapor(Y, lags = 1, k = 5, rank = 3,
             nrun = 3000, burn = 1500, thin = 5, seed = 1)
fit
```

The returned object contains posterior draws and the posterior-mean precision:

```{r structure}
str(fit, max.level = 1)
```

Key components:

- `fit$Omega` -- the `p x p` posterior-mean innovation precision matrix.
- `fit$B` -- a `p x p x n_draws` array of VAR coefficient draws.
- `fit$Lambda` -- the factor-loading draws.
- `fit$dims`, `fit$settings` -- dimensions and sampler settings.

## Recover the precision matrix

The posterior-mean precision is in `fit$Omega`. We compare it to the truth.

```{r omega}
Omega_hat <- fit$Omega

# Frobenius distance to the truth
frob <- sqrt(sum((Omega_hat - Omega_true)^2))
cat(sprintf("Frobenius ||Omega_hat - Omega_true|| = %.2f\n", frob))
```

```{r omega-heatmap, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(2,2,2,1))
image(Omega_true[, p:1], main = "True Omega",  axes = FALSE, col = hcl.colors(50, "Blue-Red"))
image(Omega_hat[, p:1],  main = "VAPOR Omega", axes = FALSE, col = hcl.colors(50, "Blue-Red"))
par(op)
```

## Extract the VAR coefficients

The posterior-mean `B` (the dynamics) is obtained by averaging the draws.

```{r coef}
B_hat <- apply(fit$B, c(1, 2), mean)
dim(B_hat)

# one-step-ahead forecast from the last observation
y_last <- Y[nrow(Y), ]
y_forecast <- as.numeric(B_hat %*% y_last)
head(y_forecast)
```

## Nowcasting: borrowing strength across series

VAPOR's precision matrix can reconstruct a held-out subset of series from the
observed ones in the same period, via the Gaussian conditional mean
`y_hidden = -Omega_hh^{-1} Omega_ho y_observed`. This uses only `Omega`.

```{r nowcast}
Omega <- fit$Omega
nowcast <- function(Omega, y_obs, obs, hid)
   as.numeric(-solve(Omega[hid, hid]) %*% Omega[hid, obs] %*% y_obs)

# hide 30% of series in the last period, predict from the rest
set.seed(2)
hid <- sort(sample(p, floor(0.3 * p)))
obs <- setdiff(seq_len(p), hid)
y   <- Y[nrow(Y), ]

pred <- nowcast(Omega, y[obs], obs, hid)
mspe <- mean((y[hid] - pred)^2)
cat(sprintf("Nowcast MSPE on held-out series: %.3f\n", mspe))
```

## Notes on usage

- **Rank.** Use `rank = "full"` when `T` comfortably exceeds `p`; use a small
  integer `rank` (e.g. 2--5) when `T` is close to `p`, where the full VAR
  overfits.
- **k (factors).** The number of precision factors. Choose by held-out
  prediction; performance typically plateaus once `k` is large enough to
  capture the dominant factors.
- **Priors on B.** `prior_B = "dl"` (default) applies Dirichlet-Laplace
  shrinkage; `"ridge"` and `"mgps"` are alternatives, the latter letting the
  effective rank emerge from the posterior under a generous rank ceiling.
